meta.title: Operation of Vacuum Oven in Pharmacognosy Laboratory

sections.purpose: To dry heat-sensitive plant extracts, crude drugs, and phytochemical isolates at low temperatures under reduced pressure, preventing thermal degradation of labile compounds.
sections.scope: Applicable to Pharmacognosy laboratory for drying volatile-rich extracts, thermolabile glycosides, alkaloids, and essential oil-containing drugs where conventional oven drying causes decomposition.
procedure: Inspect the vacuum oven door gasket, vacuum gauge, and connection ports for integrity before use.
Switch on the vacuum oven and set the required temperature: typically 40–60°C for heat-sensitive extracts.
Allow the chamber to reach the set temperature before loading samples.
Spread the extract or powder samples in thin layers on flat SS trays or Petri dishes — do not use plastic containers that may off-gas under vacuum.
Place trays inside the oven chamber, ensuring they do not obstruct the vacuum inlet port.
Close the oven door firmly and ensure the latch is secure.
Connect the vacuum pump outlet pipe to the oven vacuum inlet.
Switch on the vacuum pump and open the vacuum valve slowly — monitor the vacuum gauge.
Draw vacuum to the required level: typically 50–100 mbar (0.5–1 bar vacuum) for gentle drying.
Allow drying to proceed for the specified time (typically 3–6 hours for extracts).
Monitor temperature and vacuum level periodically; log readings in the logbook.
At the end of drying: first switch off the vacuum pump; then slowly bleed air back into the chamber using the bleed valve — never open the door while under vacuum.
Wait until the vacuum gauge reads 0 (atmospheric pressure) before opening the door.
Remove samples using tongs — surfaces may be warm.
Weigh the dried samples immediately and calculate yield / loss on drying.
Switch off the oven; clean the chamber interior with a dry cloth.
Record temperature, vacuum level, duration, material, and result in the equipment logbook.
precautions: Never open the vacuum oven door while under vacuum — pressure differential causes violent air inrush and can scatter samples.
Always bleed air back in slowly through the bleed valve before opening — rapid venting can blow fine powders out of trays.
Do not use solvent-wet samples in a vacuum oven without first ensuring the solvent is not flammable — vapours under vacuum with an electrical heat element are an explosion risk.
Regularly check and replace the door gasket — worn gaskets prevent adequate vacuum.
Do not exceed the rated maximum temperature or vacuum level of the oven.
Inspect the vacuum pump oil level and condition monthly; replace oil per manufacturer schedule.
Do not place highly corrosive materials inside — they damage the stainless steel chamber.
